problem: Existing VLN-CE methods rely on static or flat maps, heuristic goal planners and VLMs without structured environment representations, so they struggle with long-horizon navigation, cluttered scenes and unseen environments.
motivation: Humans navigate with hierarchical spatial representations (objects, regions, zones). Long-horizon VLN-CE needs structured scene understanding, principled goal selection that balances semantic relevance and reachability, and robust obstacle-avoiding control.
key_idea: Build a dynamic VLM-annotated hierarchical scene graph (object/region/zone), pick long-term goals with a Sinkhorn optimal-transport planner trading off instruction relevance and geodesic cost, and execute them with a GCN-based PPO low-level policy.
insight: The ablations attribute the gains roughly evenly across components: removing the hierarchy drops R2R-CE SR from 0.64 to 0.57, removing OT to 0.59, removing graph-aware control to 0.56, and removing VLM descriptions to 0.58. Caveat: the OT cost matrix is diagonal (infinite off-diagonal), so the 'OT' reduces to a per-node scoring/argmax, and the claimed optimality theorem is trivial. The baseline numbers appear to be round and suspiciously uniform, and the baselines are a weak or non-standard set (no ETPNav, DUET-style or other strong VLN-CE SOTA), so the SOTA claim should be treated cautiously.
method: Object-level graph: Grounded-SAM detects objects, depth is projected to 3D using pose, LLaVA-OneVision writes descriptions, SigLIP provides features.
Region-level aggregation: spectral clustering (normalized cut) over a Gaussian-kernel graph combining 3D distance and text-embedding similarity (sigma=0.5, lambda=0.2, 1.5 m threshold).

Zone-level integration: connectivity-seeded region merging into zones (kitchen, bedroom), with a VLM judging whether adjacent regions belong to the same zone; the graph is updated online by matching nodes on distance and feature similarity.

OT topological planner: relevance s_i = max cosine of instruction token embeddings (BERT) vs node description; cost = geodesic distance + alpha*frontier penalty - beta*s_i; Sinkhorn solves the transport plan and goal = argmax T_ii; Dijkstra gives the topological path.

Graph-aware low-level control: 3-layer GCN over the local subgraph plus SigLIP visual features, pose and next subgoal feed an MLP policy trained with PPO (rewards: +1 subgoal, -0.01*dist, -1 collision); a Tryout heuristic handles blocked FORWARD actions.
Training: VLM and GCN pre-trained on Matterport3D, then fine-tuned on R2R-CE/RxR-CE with student forcing, loss = imitation NLL + 0.1 * PPO loss.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-OneVision (VLM, fine-tuned), SigLIP, Grounded-SAM, BERT text encoder, 3-layer GCN + MLP PPO policy
setting.training_data: Matterport3D pre-training for VLM (contrastive image-text) and GCN (edge prediction); fine-tuning on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, 100,000 episodes, 8 A100 GPUs
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30° spacing) plus pose (x,y,theta)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP, with high-level topological goal nodes
setting.privileged: pose provided by simulator; no other stated privileged info

numbers.extra: Pre-trained on Matterport3D; SR/SPL/OSR printed as fractions

results: HSAN reports R2R-CE val-unseen SR 0.64 / SPL 0.59 / NE 3.28 / OSR 0.71, beating the best listed baseline LLaVA-Nav (0.58/0.53/3.62/0.65), and RxR-CE SR 0.59 vs 0.53. It also leads on the multilingual and high-clutter subsets (SR 0.57 and 0.61).
limitations: Computational overhead of real-time graph construction (stated by the authors).

Baselines are weak or outdated and omit modern VLN-CE SOTA; there is no real-robot evaluation and no released code; the OT formulation degenerates to a diagonal assignment, so the theoretical optimality claim adds little.
Reported step budgets are inconsistent (15/25 vs 150/250) and relies on simulator pose.
